title: Deep convolutional network detects COVID-19 pneumonia on chest radiographs
summary: A deep convolutional neural network was trained on public radiographs (8,851 normal, 6,045 pneumonia, 200 COVID-19), with 13,586 images for training and 1510 for testing. Sensitivity was 96.8% and positive predictive value 90.9%. In external validation it identified 174 of 204 radiographs (85%) from 107 confirmed COVID-19 patients; in 50 immunocompromised leukemia patients the AI probability correlated with suggestive features. The COVID-19 training class is small and labels come from public data.
ai_technology: Deep convolutional neural network classifying chest radiographs for COVID-19 pneumonia
organization: Tokyo Medical and Dental University; The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center

evidence.tested: Held-out test images plus two external validations (107 confirmed COVID-19 patients, and 50 patients with leukemia).
evidence.unknown: Clinical usefulness beyond the pandemic setting; label quality of the public training data; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: A CNN classified chest radiographs as COVID-19 pneumonia.
